article: [ Wrote this awhile back for a collaborative writing forum I work with. Enjoy. ] The defendant stood stoically in the courtroom, seemingly unconcerned with what hung in the balance. Absently, he checked his watch. 12:30 PM. It was time. He nudged his lawyer, whispered something; the man nodded solemnly. This seemed to please him, as he returned to facing the bench. After an interminable pause, a door opened, and the twenty men of the jury entered, seating themselves in the benches provided for them. The judge, an elderly man with a severe look about him, adjusted his wig and cast one last hard glare at the defendant before rapping his gavel, seating the assembled audience. "Anton Malinowski, you will rise to hear verdict," he said, his voice solemn, clear, imperious. Malinowski, the defendant, stood in defiance, his entire being tensed as he glared unflinchingly at the man who had been his tormenter, his adversary, for the past two months. It had all come down to this moment. "Has the jury reached a verdict?," the judge said, turning his attentions away from the Communist before him. "We have, Your Honor," came a voice from the bench, a woman's this time. "Very well," the judge replied. "You may proceed." "In the first count, of Treason against the Government of His Majesty the King, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty," the woman read. "The vote upon this matter was unanimous." Malinowski's glance snapped to the bench, staring daggers at those who shrank beneath the man's gaze. His lawyer placed a hand upon his shoulder, a vain attempt to calm the man. The woman proceeded, her voice cracking now. "In the second matter, of ten counts Murder in the First Degree, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty. Upon these counts, the votes were unanimous." "In the third matter, of eighty-three counts Defamation of the Personage of the King, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty. Upon these counts, the votes were unanimous." Having finished her labor, the woman sat, heaving a sigh. Malinowski was rendered numb as the judge thanked the jury for its service. He was numb as the judge read out that he was to be executed by hanging. He was deaf and blind to the fury of the crowd assembled outside the courthouse and throughout the country. As he was led away in handcuffs and irons, he was ignorant of the one fact that would make Anton Malinowski, steelworker, a name remembered throughout history. He had started the Revolution. "Fuck, we can't hold'em! Where the fuck is our cavalry?" Officer Fabian Wyrick screamed in desperation into his radio as hordes of enraged protestors converged upon him. The shield wall of the Greater Glodno Police, Special Services Division, had seemed so imposing when the two sides had merely been casting harsh looks and harsh words at one another. Then, the verdict had come, and the words turned to action. Hundreds, perhaps a thousand, rushed toward the courthouse and toward the police barrier, trying to break their man free or at least break a few heads in the process. The police quickly found themselves overwhelmed. Wyrick swung wildly in all directions, making contact at least a few times before his stamina and adrenaline high wore off. Exhausted, and having made no serious dent in the mob before him, he relented. In an instant, the mob set upon him, furiously beating themselves against the riot shield behind which he had crouched, and beating him ferociously with any instrument they could set their hands upon. This was how it would end. Wyrick closed his eyes and began praying for grace, for mercy, for forgiveness of any sins, waiting for the moment to come when it would end. And end it did, though in a most horrible way. Suddenly, a loud revving sound cut through the din, causing police and protestor alike to stop and turn their heads. Advancing down the block, unmistakable in its behemoth size and terrible glory, was a BTR-80. The Royal Army had apparently decided to take matters into its own hands, and proceeded to unleash a torrent of 7.62mm fire and 14.5mm heavy autocannon rounds into the now-fleeing crowd. Most did not have time to scream before they were cut down. Wyrick could only watch, horrified, as the crew of the BTR chased after those who fled, running several down in a splatter of gore. "You fucking monsters!," he shouted, knowing as he did that it was all in vain. "Stop this fucking slaughter! For the love of God stop it!" Not thinking, half-mad with rage, he charged the BTR. It was by sheer luck that he managed to climb atop it, and sheer forgetfulness of the crew that he managed to pop the compartment open. Now, he found himself staring face-first at uniformed crew of one of the Household Guard's armored carriers. It was not a situation most would envy. "What the fuck do you think you're doing? Those are our countrymen out there you goddamn psychopaths! Turn this fucking thing around and go home!" It was futile, he knew, but Wyrick was a man on autopilot, and futility did not register at this point. After a pause, Wyrick received his reply in the form of a solid slug to the jaw. article: Polya urns are urns where at each unit of time a ball is drawn and is replaced with some other balls according to its colour. We introduce a more general model: The replacement rule depends on the colour of the drawn ball and the value of the time (mod p). We discuss some intriguing properties of the differential operators associated to the generating functions encoding the evolution of these urns. The initial partial differential equation indeed leads to ordinary linear differential equations and we prove that the moment generating functions are D-finite. For a subclass, we exhibit a closed form for the corresponding generating functions (giving the exact state of the urns at time n). When the time goes to infinity, we show that these periodic Polya urns follow a rich variety of behaviours: their asymptotic fluctuations are described by a family of distributions, the generalized Gamma distributions, which can also be seen as powers of Gamma distributions. En passant, we establish some enumerative links with other combinatorial objects, and we give an application for a new result on the asymptotics of Young tableaux: This approach allows us to prove that the law of the lower right corner in a triangular Young tableau follows asymptotically a product of generalized Gamma distributions.

article: I feel like I'm drowning in work. At times like this, I can't help but think back and ponder about how I came to hold this position. I stare with resentment at the placard sitting at the edge of my desk. Brian Colms - God of Oil - Divinity Corp. I took a position here at Divinity as an intern in my senior year. I was a political science major; simulated evolutionary engineering was nowhere near my radar as a potential career path. The opportunity at Divinity arose because I knew a guy that knew a guy. I figured it would be a good way to beef up my CV. Twelve years later, and I hate my life more than ever. I know what you're asking: "If this job isn't for you, why did you continue after your internship?" Fair question. Allow me to elaborate. Divinity is a leading innovator in the global evolutionary engineering sector. Basically, we create multiverses; simulations of millions of constantly evolving universes at a time generating thousands unique worlds that harbor simulated life and we harvest the technological outcomes of these worlds for real-world applications. When I began as an intern, I was tasked with cataloging a subset of hydrophobic substances. For the most part, the work was pretty minimal. In fact, the brunt of it had already been done before I got here. I simply had to keep an eye on the development of new oils as they popped into existence in each simulation. After graduation, I was looking for work. As luck would have it, Divinity was now hiring demi-gods to be in charge of its expanding oil sims. So I applied for the position and I got it. Initially, the job was similar to my work as an intern; some mineral oils here, a few triglycerides there. I couldn't understand why they wanted a person to take on this position full-time. But I wasn't complaining. The pay was decent and the work was manageable. So I stuck with it and gradually worked my way up the ranks over the years. As this area began to expand, so too did the workload, and I had to take on some interns, myself, to help get some things done. But it wasn't until my fifth year that things began to snowball out of control. I know the planet that was the source of it all. I know it well. It haunts my dreams. When I close my eyes, I see the architecture of their damned oil refineries with vividness. They use it daily; some of it for cooking and some of it for transportation. They wage wars for some of it. Entire political battles revolve around the stuff. Fucking Earth. For the previous decade that Divinity and other evolutionary engineering firms had been operating, never had a single simulation found such extensive uses for the stuff. But Earth had, and it was like they were addicted to it. When I realized what was happening, I tried to change the source code for the program to try to get them to use something else to drive their civilization. I gave them nuclear. Let one of the administrator gods deal with the issue. But they only used it as a deterrent to help keep their oil businesses running. I strengthened the coding of their wind turbines. Jim, the asshole God of wind could take care of it. Nope. Solar, I figured, would surely provide a strong enough incentive for them to switch. article: The flexibility of the inference process in Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) has recently led to revising traditional probabilistic topic models giving rise to Neural Topic Models (NTM). VAEs and NTMs are particularly useful for text data, where the goal is to discover the underlying topics that are present in the corpus. In a VAE, the model is trained to reconstruct the input data and generate new samples by learning a compressed representation of the data in a lower-dimensional latent space. The approach is unsupervised, meaning that the model does not have access to any labels. In contrast, an NTM takes a similar approach but uses a neural network to represent the topic model. The model learns to represent the topics as a distribution of words, and the generative process is conditioned on both the topic and a document-specific distribution. Overall, these models provide a powerful framework for discovering the latent structure of text data, allowing for improved modeling and analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets.

article: At the heart of machine learning lies the question of generalizability of learned rules over previously unseen data. While over-parameterized models based on neural networks are now ubiquitous in machine learning, they can suffer from overfitting, where the model has learned to fit the training data so closely that it is unable to accurately predict on new, unseen data. Regularization techniques, such as L1 and L2 regularization, dropout, and early stopping, can be used to help prevent overfitting and improve generalization. Other approaches to improving generalization include data augmentation, where the training data is artificially expanded by creating new examples from existing ones (such as rotating, flipping, and scaling images), and ensemble methods, which combine the predictions of multiple models to improve accuracy and reduce overfitting. Overall, the ability of a model to generalize to previously unseen data is a critical aspect of its performance, and techniques to address this issue should be carefully considered when designing and training machine learning models.

However, I think that it happens as a result of pure luck. It is a difficult play to turn, but in almost every case, (the sample size is small) there are men on 1st and 2nd, and then there is sharp line drive directly to the shortstop or 2nd baseman. Now, the 5-4-3 triple play requires men on first and second, plus a hard ground ball directly to third. This again, is all luck and circumstance, but after that, the third baseman has to field the ground ball and tag third base, and execute a flawless throw to second. The second basemen must then make the catch, tag, exchange the ball from glove to hand and throw flawlessly and immediately to first, where the first baseman must make the catch and tag. So, I think while both of these plays essentially have to be served to the defense on a silver platter, the 5-4-3 triple play has many more degrees of freedom, thus making it a much more difficult play to execute when available. article: In point-based sensing systems such as coordinate measuring machines (CMM) and laser ultrasonics where complete sensing is impractical due to the high sensing time and cost, adaptive sensing through a systematic exploration is vital for online inspection and anomaly quantification. However, in many anomaly quantification applications, the main goal is to estimate sparse anomalous regions in the pixel-level accurately. In this paper, we develop a novel framework named Adaptive Kernelized Maximum-Minimum Distance (AKM 2 D) to speed up the inspection and anomaly detection process through an intelligent sequential sampling scheme integrated with fast estimation and detection. The proposed method balances the sampling efforts between the space-filling sampling (exploration) and focused sampling near the anomalous region (exploitation). The proposed methodology is validated by conducting simulations and a case study of anomaly detection in composite sheets using a guided wave test.

article: Image forgery localization is a very active and open research field for the difficulty to handle the large variety of manipulations a malicious user can perform by means of more and more sophisticated image processing techniques. The goal of image forgery localization is to automatically detect and localize the areas of the image that have been manipulated. This is important for a wide range of applications, including forensics, copyright protection, and content authentication. There are various techniques employed for image forgery localization, but some of the popular ones include: 1. Copy-Move Forgery Detection: This method is used to detect and localize the region of an image in which a part has been copied and pasted, either within the same image or from another image. 2. Splicing Forgery Detection: This technique is used in cases where parts of one image have been spliced into another image. This method is used when we suspect that multiple images were used to create a single image that has been altered. 3. Retouching Forgery Detection: In this method, the focus is on detecting areas of an image that were retouched or modified using software tools like clone stamp or a healing brush. 4. Compression Artifact Analysis: Certain artifacts are created during image compression, and the analysis of these artifacts can help detect image manipulation. Overall, image forgery localization is an important field of research that is continuously advancing as image manipulation techniques continue to evolve.

article: In the spirit of full disclosure, I will announce at the start of this post that I am a white male, who has had (admittedly) a healthy amount of privilege I love moments in my life in which my beliefs are challenged (thus the reason I love this sub), but a friend on Facebook recently posted this quote (from Scott Woods) which set me on a personal moral confusion spiral: Racism is a complex system of social and political levers and pulleys set up generations ago to continue working on the behalf of some, at the expense of others. Racism is an insidious cultural disease. It is so insidious that it doesn't care if you are a white person who likes black people; it's still going to find a way to infect how you deal with people who don't look like you. Yes, racism looks like hate, but hate is just one manifestation. Privilege is another. Access is another. Ignorance is another. Apathy is another. And so on. So while I agree with people who say no one is born racist, it remains a powerful system that we're immediately born into. It's like being born into air: you take it in as soon as you breathe. It's not a cold that you can get over. There is no anti-racist certification class. It's a set of socioeconomic traps and cultural values that are fired up every time we interact with the world. It is a thing you have to keep scooping out of the boat of your life to keep from drowning in it. Now, I completely agree that racism is a highly complex issue, and the elimination of racism means far more than the elimination of personal prejudice, it involves the elimination of centuries of socio-economic, political and cultural mechanisms that benefit some to the detriment of others. But I find myself having trouble internalizing that racism is "like being born in to air," and that "it's not a cold [I] can get over." Yes, I have been born in to a culture that is racist - there is no denying this. But, to me, scooping the water out of the boat of my otherwise unconscious prejudice is what I believe makes me deserving of being able to say I'm not racist. I don't agree than no matter what I do, I'm a racist, and my only choice is to keep chipping away, all the while merely accepting that when I step outside I'll be firing up the cultural machine of racism I swim in. I believe there is "anti-racism certification," and it manifests itself in beliefs and actions that demonstrate the absence of prejudice. I whole-heartedly believe that all human beings are born equal. In fact, I don't really believe in the idea of race. Obviously I understand that it exists as a social construct, but I believe that anyone who understand what DNA is, how genetic mutation works, and how little we differ from any other member of our species should laugh at the idea of race. I try to act every day in a way that rejects prejudice, and shows a love and respect for all humanity, regardless of gender, race, etc.. I have no doubt found myself struggling against engrained social and cultural mechanisms that would persuade me otherwise, were I to give in to them unconsciously, but I believe the fact that I think about this, and struggle with my beliefs and my actions and how they contribute to the disease of racism around me, and actively change when confronted with the fact that what I believe is wrong, should grant me the privilege of being able to say that I am not a racist, and the suggestion that I am, without any hope of changing that, upsets me very much. Is there something I'm not understanding about this argument? Am I just straight up wrong about this?

article: Adversarial training has been recently employed for realizing structured semantic segmentation, in which the aim is to preserve higher-level scene structural consistencies in dense predictions. However, as we show, value-based discrimination between the predictions from the segmentation network and ground-truth annotations can hinder the training process from learning to improve structural qualities as well as disabling the network from properly expressing uncertainties. In this paper, we rethink adversarial training for semantic segmentation and propose to formulate the fakereal discrimination framework with a correctincorrect training objective. More specifically, we replace the discriminator with a "gambler" network that learns to spot and distribute its budget in areas where the predictions are clearly wrong, while the segmenter network tries to leave no clear clues for the gambler where to bet. Empirical evaluation on two road-scene semantic segmentation tasks shows that not only does the proposed method re-enable expressing uncertainties, it also improves pixel-wise and structure-based metrics.

article: We consider probabilistic model checking for continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) induced from Stochastic Reaction Networks (SRNs) against a fragment of Continuous Stochastic Logic (CSL) extended with reward operators. Classical numerical algorithms for CSL model checking based on uniformisation are limited to finite CTMCs and suffer from exponential growth of the state space with respect to the number of species. On the other hand, approximate techniques such as mean-field approximations and simulations combined with statistical inference are more scalable, but can be time consuming and do not support the full expressiveness of CSL. In this paper we employ a continuous-space approximation of the CTMC in terms of a Gaussian process based on the Central Limit Approximation (CLA), also known as the Linear Noise Approximation (LNA), whose solution requires solving a number of differential equations that is quadratic in the number of species and independent of the population size. We then develop efficient and scalable approximate model checking algorithms on the resulting Gaussian process, where we restrict the target regions for probabilistic reachability to convex polytopes. This allows us to derive an abstraction in terms of a time-inhomogeneous discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC), whose dimension is independent of the number of species, on which model checking is performed. Using results from probability theory, we prove the convergence in distribution of our algorithms to the corresponding measures on the original CTMC. We implement the techniques and, on a set of examples, demonstrate that they allow us to overcome the state space explosion problem, while still correctly characterizing the stochastic behaviour of the system. Our methods can be used for formal analysis of a wide range of distributed stochastic systems, including biochemical systems, sensor networks and population protocols.

article: By making it an odd number, it makes it more difficult for your sleep addled mind to do the math of "I hit my snooze twice, can I hit it again and still be on time to work?" By forcing your brain to do more complex calculations, it helps wake your brain up. So by helping you snooze, it also serves the purpose of getting you out of bed in the long run. Also, by making it 9 minutes, when you finally do roll out of bed, you actually have a little bit more time than you expected (since your sleep addled brain is just going to round to ten anyway when trying to do sleepytime snooze math). It's a win-win.','URL0 The most likely explanation: In the days of dial clocks, the snooze interval was originally intended to be ten minutes max, but precision was unimportant and engineers were content if they could make the interval nine minutes and change. When the industry switched to digital, clock designers figured the standard snooze interval was nine minutes; "and change" went out the window. Now we're getting somewhere. Partial confirmation of this view comes from Jay "Pappy" Kennan, a clock collector who took apart an old GE electromechanical clock with one of the earliest snooze buttons. The clock's snooze-gear mechanism was not precise; the snooze interval could be anywhere from nine to nine and a half minutes. Pappy's opinion, seconded by a clock engineer, was that the original, none-too-ambitious designers wanted a clock with a snooze interval in the nine-to-ten-minute range. So what may have happened was, some early chip designer inspected an old mechanical clock with a snooze button, figured that a nine-minute snooze interval had been ordained by the clock gods, and built it into his chipand we've been stuck with it ever since. That's my theory, and I'm sticking to it.

If the third toss is tails, you receive an additional payout of 8 dollars (for a total of 10 dollars) and the game is over. article: To increase the computational efficiency of interest-point based object retrieval, researchers have put remarkable research efforts into improving the efficiency of k NN-based feature matching, pursuing to match thousands of features against a database within fractions of a second. However, due to the high-dimensional nature of image features that reduces the effectivity of index structures (curse of dimensionality), due to the vast amount of features stored in image databases (images are often represented by up to several thousand features), this ultimate goal demanded to trade query runtimes for query precision. In this paper we address an approach complementary to indexing in order to improve the runtimes of retrieval by querying only the most promising keypoint descriptors, as this affects matching runtimes linearly and can therefore lead to increased efficiency. As this reduction of k NN queries reduces the number of tentative correspondences, a loss of query precision is minimized by an additional image-level correspondence generation stage with a computational performance independent of the underlying indexing structure. We evaluate such an adaption of the standard recognition pipeline on a variety of datasets using both SIFT and state-of-the-art binary descriptors. Our results suggest that decreasing the number of queried descriptors does not necessarily imply a reduction in the result quality as long as alternative ways of increasing query recall (by thoroughly selecting k) and MAP (using image-level correspondence generation) are considered.

article: The potassium and sodium ion concentrations are what cause the neuron to fire. Or actually they allow the action potential to propagate along the nerve. A nerve cell starts off at a resting state with a negative charge inside and positive charge outside the cell membrane. When a signal is received, sodium ions rush into the cell causing a rapid depolarization and a shift to a positive charge inside the cell. This then triggers the opening of potassium ion channels, allowing potassium ions to flow out of the cell, which repolarizes the cell back to a negative charge again. This movement of ions creates an electrical signal that travels along the length of the neuron, allowing for the transmission of the signal from one neuron to the next.

Our only means of control is to set surge prices, then taxicabsand passengers maximize their utilities subject to these prices. We study tworelated models: a continuous passenger-taxicab setting, similar to the Wardropmodel, and a discrete passenger-taxicab setting. In the continuous setting,every location is occupied by a set of infinitesimal strategic taxicabs and aset of infinitesimal non-strategic passengers. In the discrete setting everylocation is occupied by a set of strategic agents, taxicabs and passengers,passengers have differing values for service. We expand the continuous model toa time-dependent setting and study the corresponding online environment. Surge prices are in passenger-taxicab equilibrium if there exists a min costflow that moves taxicabs about such that (a) every taxicab follows a bestresponse, (b) all strategic passengers at v with value above the surge pricerv for v, are served and (c) no strategic passengers with value belowrv are served (non-strategic infinitesimal passengers are always served). This paper computes surge prices such that resulting passenger-taxicabequilibrium maximizes social welfare, and the computation of such surge pricesis in poly time. Moreover, it is a dominant strategy for passengers to revealtheir true values. We seek to maximize social welfare in the online environment, and derivetight competitive ratio bounds to this end. article: I'm guessing the the Mercedes engine is turbosupercharged and the Mustang engine is not.,A lot of comments already hit on this but I'll take a shot at it. The way engines work is fairly simple. The piston moves down, pulling in air. That air is mixed with an appropriate amount of fuel and the valve (how the air got in) is closed. The piston goes back up and compresses the mixed air and fuel and then a spark makes it all explode. The explosion pushes the piston back down, then a different valve (exhaust) opens and when the piston comes back up it forces all of the waste from the process out. This is grossly simplified but you get the idea. There are a lot of ways to make more power but it mostly comes down to creating bigger explosions or creating more explosions. More is simple: either use more pistons (making the actual engine much larger and harder to fit in the car) or spin the motor faster (requiring much tighter tolerances, lighter materials, and a LOT of careful design to make sure fuel is being burned at the right ratio to prevent potential catastrophe). Both of these options require a considerably higher amount of fuel, even when the motor isn't working as hard. The other option is creating bigger explosions. You have to make sure that you use the right amount of both air and fuel in order to keep things working properly so you have to increase both to make the explosions more powerful. Fuel is easy, air is complicated. That's where "forced induction" comes in. Things like "Ram Air injection," superchargers, and turbochargers increase the air coming into the motor in different ways. Ram air forces in more air due to the speed of the vehicle traveling. Its cheap and easy, but is sensitive to altitude and air density (temperature and air pressure) and isn't a tremendous gain. Superchargers run on a belt driven by the motor. This increases the amount of work that the motor has to do all the time so it can actually see very little gains at lower speeds. Turbochargers run off of the waste gas created by the motor. This gas spins a turbine at a high rate of speed forcing dramatically higher amounts of air in. The upside of this is that because if how its powered you don't see the typical downsides if a supercharger (working harder at low speeds) but you do see the benefits. Turbocharging a motor at 1 bar (about 14.5 psi) is effectively doubling the amount of air the motor is able to work with, enabling it to act as a motor twice its size when it needs to but operate like a regular motor in normal use. The big downsides here are that turbochargers are expensive and have a lot of "packaging" (fitting the turbocharger and the necessary piping to make it work) concerns. They also got off to a rocky start in use in america, so many people were turned off of them due to concerns about expensive repairs and reliability. Modern systems are far more reliable and effective so there has been a big increase in their use recently. There's a lot more to it than that, of course. Engine dynamics are a bit more complicated (how the motor feels and sounds throughout its operating range and if that matches the character the designers have in mind). Ford does have a turbocharged 4 cylinder model coming out later this year to split the performance gap between the 300 horsepower v6 and the 435 horsepower v8. They've even done turbocharged 4 cylinder motors in traditionally v8 cars in the past (Mustang SVO and the Thunderbird Turbocoupe) with some critical success but not much sales success. "Honey, NOW!" his mother yelled, he hadn't realized he'd been sitting there stunned. Her yell snapped him back to reality where his training kicked in, he sprung from his bed, far more controlled now without the ice water spurring his movements, and was inside his closet almost instantly. With a pleased nod, his mother hopped the banister behind her to the first floor and was gone, likely to toss her pack in the "truck" and grab anything they may have extra room for. He tried to don his gear swiftly, the way he'd been taught, but nervousness had an icy grip on his chest in a way his training hadn't prepared him for. As such, he tripped while trying to pull his other pant-leg up, landing in a pile of dirty clothes, with his cap on, his green shirt around his neck like a scarf, and an 80lb duffel bag over one shoulder making him feel like a turtle that some petulant child had flipped. "There must have been a tremor or something, was that what shook the bed?" Realizing he was standing like a doe in the headights, Liam mentally berated his internal monologue. Instead, the windows began to shake violently and the ear-splitting sound of a sonic boom cascaded through the house, snapping Liam out of his self-reverie. He hopped the banister, landing on the floor below in a crouch, feeling the impact shockwaves cascade through his lower extremities and wishing he had thrown his bag over first, the extra weight made the landing unexpectedly rough. Liam stood and looked around, taking in his childhood home for, most likely, the last time. It almost felt as if it were sucking him in, not physically, but mentally, dragging his mind away from his body. As he noticed what was happening to him, the tug on his mind intensified, the more he fought against it, the more agonizing it got and, before he knew it, he heard screaming. article: There are several ways to purify water: filtration, and distillation, and chemicals (bleach, iodine, etc.) Filtration uses filters of different porosities to remove particles (sand, etc.) and microorganisms (bacteria, etc.). A filter that's 0.1 micro-meters (microns) will pretty much remove all the bacteria and most of the particles, because they're 5 - 10 microns in size. Distillation heats up the water until it boils or evaporates, then passes the water through a cold tube to turn it back into a liquid. Contaminants that are in the water (particles, bacteria, etc.) can't evaporate and remain behind. Distillation is considered "better" than filtration, because boiling the water kills the bacteria; with filters, the bacteria are caught by the filter but are still alive and can multiply and possibly contaminate the filtered water. Chemical methods rely on adding a chemical that will kill bacteria, such as chlorine bleach or iodine. This chemical is effective at killing bacteria at doses that aren't too dangerous for humans.

article: I wasn't sure why my mother had never mentioned the VHS tapes she had stashed away in the bottom of her bedroom closet. I was only rooting around in there because I'd loaned her some shoes last time I'd come home from college and I wanted them back, but instead I found about a dozen unlabeled tapes stacked neatly in the back corner behind the pile of shoes and mostly hidden by some long dresses. At first I thought they were going to be weird sex tapes or something, but when curiosity compelled me to put one in the VHS player my parents still had lying around, I found that they were of a different nature altogether. The first tape started off with a grainy view of our living room. It was Christmastime according to the decorated tree beside the fireplace and the wreath sitting on the mantle, partially obscuring the large mirror behind it. After a few moments a woman came onscreen carrying a small baby. It took me a long moment to recognize her as my mother, and I was only certain of her identity when I heard her voice say "Look, Ashley, Santa Claus came!" Ashley is my name, so I assumed the baby in her arms must have been me. My birthday is in September, so this must have been my first Christmas. I watched transfixed as a part of my past that I had no chance of remembering played out before me. I got some new pajamas and a few baby toys that year, and most of the tape was just me snuggling in my mother's arms while she tried to get me to play with a stuffed elephant. Eventually I started getting fussy, and my mother got up and took me out of the room. After a few moments the living room scene went staticky, and I fast forwarded a bit to make sure that it wasn't just a blank spot in this homemade tape, but that seemed to be the end of the recording. I quickly popped the next tape in. This one started in the same manner: a view of our living room without anyone in it. There was no Christmas tree this time. The scene remained unmoved for longer than the first one, but eventually a toddler came running into the room laughing hysterically. It was me again, and close behind me was my mother. I fell to the floor, still giggling, and my mother immediately scooped me up and spun me around, also laughing. She played with me a bit, tickling me, blowing raspberries at me, and tossing me up in the air, all the while laughing with me amidst my screams of excitement. " Come on, silly girl, we need to get you dressed! " she said finally. " Noooooooo! " squealed the still pajama-clad toddler, but I made no moves to resist as my mother carried me back the way we came. Again the scene remained still for a time before going staticky, and again I found that that was the end of the video, despite there being hours of recording time left on the tape. I was starting to feel like something was a little strange about these tapes, but I kept watching them. Each captured between five to fifteen minute snippets of my childhood, not always in order. There was another Christmas scene, and a birthday party, but most of them were just regular days, always filmed from the same angle in our living room. However, something in the seventh one caught my attention. The large mirror above the fireplace was directly opposite a bay window looking out into the front yard. From the angle that the camera was at, I could clearly see the front yard through the window reflected in the mirror. The young me in the video was doing something in the living room as usual, but some movement in the yard drew my eyes up to the mirror. It was just our dog running around, but as I was about to look back to myself in the living room, the realization hit me like a ton of bricks. Where was the camera? From this angle I should have been able to see the camera in the mirror, but there was nothing there. I tried to convince myself that I was wrong, that the camera was shorter than the window and out of view of the mirror, but I couldn't. I had literally just finished my college trigonometry midterms the week prior and passed with flying colors. I had a natural talent for visualizing this stuff, and I knew beyond a shadow of a doubt that I should be able to see the recording device in that mirror. article: The PARAFAC2 is a multimodal factor analysis model suitable for analyzing multi-way data when one of the modes has incomparable observation units, for example because of differences in signal sampling or batch sizes. A fully probabilistic treatment of the PARAFAC2 is desirable in order to improve robustness to noise and provide a well founded principle for determining the number of factors, but challenging because the factor loadings are constrained to be orthogonal. We develop two probabilistic formulations of the PARAFAC2 along with variational procedures for inference: In the one approach, the mean values of the factor loadings are orthogonal leading to closed form variational updates, and in the other, the factor loadings themselves are orthogonal using a matrix Von Mises-Fisher distribution. We contrast our probabilistic formulation to the conventional direct fitting algorithm based on maximum likelihood. On simulated data and real fluorescence spectroscopy and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry data, we compare our approach to the conventional PARAFAC2 model estimation and find that the probabilistic formulation is more robust to noise and model order misspecification. The probabilistic PARAFAC2 thus forms a promising framework for modeling multi-way data accounting for uncertainty.

In this case, we want to ensure that the learned probabilistic system can simulate the behavior of the positive tree samples, but not the negative tree samples. So, putting it all together, we are trying to learn a non-deterministic probabilistic system that can simulate the behavior of positive tree samples and avoid simulating the behavior of negative tree samples, consistent with the principle of strong simulation.

article: In live-streamed programming, developers broadcast their development work on open source projects using streaming media such as YouTube or Twitch. Sessions are first announced by a developer acting as the streamer, inviting other developers to join and interact as watchers using chat. We also found that streamers are motivated by knowledge sharing, socializing, and building an online identity, but face challenges with tool limitations and maintaining engagement with watchers. We discuss the implications of these findings, identify limitations with current tools, and propose design recommendations for new forms of tools to better supporting live-streamed programming.

article: "Hallo?" I heard a child's voice calling in the forest, "Hallo?" Great, I thought. Red Riding Hood's lost. But as I continued down the path, I saw that it was two unfamiliar children, headed towards the Witch's house. The children were clearly brother and sister: thin with button noses and freckles. One was a girl, in a ragged gray dress, the other a boy in suspenders. I stalked in the shadows behind them. I could smell the softened caramel of the Witch's roof tiles before the house came into view. The kids must have spotted the house too, because they stopped shouting for help, and went running so fast towards the candy house their arms flapped behind them. I paused. It was a pretty picture: the gingerbread house, framed in dark chocolate pillars. The children fell to eating it. From where I stood, in shadows at the edge of her yard, I could see the Witch inside the window. She stood when she heard their munching, and crept towards the door. The sounds of their feasting echoed throughout the forest: smacking of lips, grunts, and (most terribly of all) the crunch of the little girl's teeth against the peppermint doorknob. It was a pleasant spring day, and I had things to do. But I couldn't help but watch for a moment. I heaved my axe up against my shoulder, blade up. I straightened my spine a little and wiped my runny nose on my sleeve. A wolf appeared the Big Bad Wolf lured by the smell of the children as surely as the children were lured by the house. He was a big, dark gray wolf, with teeth as jagged as broken glass. When he smiled at the children, his lips rolled back, revealing gray gums. Interesting, I thought. Witch vs. wolf? Let's see where this goes. The witch finished creeping to the doorway. She and the wolf spotted each other, but the children kept eating, oblivious. The wolf's low growl reverberated through the handle of my axe. Yet the children, the little dummies, still didn't hear or see either of them. I wondered how long it would take them to realize they were in danger. I've always thought of myself as a highly capable person, although lately I've had a bit of a cold. I took two steps forward into the yard, when the wolf lunged at the Witch. I backed up again, hiding behind a bush. The witch and the wolf grappled, tumbling down the slope of the yard and towards the woods. Towards me, in fact. The wolf tore at the witch's dark cloak, white teeth flashing The Witch clawed back with long fingernails. Within a minute, the Witch flipped over on top and sucker-punched the wolf right in the gut. The wolf yowled and fell limp, and the Witch pulled out a knife and cut his throat. This commotion, finally, roused the children from their feast. They stared at the dead wolf, melted chocolate smeared on their faces. The Witch turned towards them. Before she could open her mouth, I threw my axe in the Witch's back. She dropped to the forest floor. (If the witch's back hadn't been turned, I wouldn't have stood a chance. I've been ill lately, and I'm weak. I'd hate to think what would happen if I had to face the wolf.) "Hey, dummies!" I stepped over the witch's dead body and nodded a greeting to the two grubby kids. They stared at me. "Why do you have an axe?" the boy asked. He looked me up and down. "I was chopping wood," I said. "But you're old." I shrugged. I was a little petite lady, it was true. I sneezed. "And you're sick." "When you live out in the middle of the woods, you've got to chop wood for your fireplace everyday," I said, "Even when you're old and sick." "Isn't there a lumberjack around here?" "He's a rip-off," I said, "His prices are too expensive. And besides, he's never around when I really need him. He always comes too late to help." I turned my head and coughed into my sleeve. Soon as I got home, I was going to take a nap. "That candy crap's no good for you," I said, "Little Red Riding Hood's on her way to visit, want to come to my house? She's bringing a basket of wholesome food with her, I'll share it with you." "Wholesome food?" the girl asked, her little teeth smeared brown with chocolate, "What's that?" "Apples and shit, you know?" I said, "C'mon. Let's go. I hope Red Riding Hood didn't get lost." I grabbed them both by the elbow and ushered them through the yard, giving the dead bodies of the Wolf and the Witch a wide berth. This is because pain nerves come in two general types; a thicker neuron with a sheath that transmits intense pain signal quickly from a small radius around the receptors in your skin, and a thinner neuron that more slowly transmits pain signals from a more general region of your body. When pressure is put on the skin, the faster pain signals can be physically blocked from reaching the brain while the slower ones pass through. So how is this all related to shaking? By quickly shaking your fingers around, you are subjecting your fingers to g-forces as they are in a constant state of acceleration and deceleration, which could potentially provide enough pressure to dull some of that initial intense pain." -uZaburino from the last time it was posted. article: We consider the problem of ranking a set of items from pairwise comparisons in the presence of features associated with the items. We introduce a new probabilistic preference model called feature-Bradley-Terry-Luce (f-BTL) model that generalizes the standard BTL model to incorporate feature information. We present a new least squares based algorithm called fBTL-LS which we show requires much lesser than O ( n log (n pairs to obtain a good ranking - precisely our new sample complexity bound is of O ( log ), where denotes the number of 'independent items' of the set, in general n . Our analysis is novel and makes use of tools from classical graph matching theory to provide tighter bounds that sheds light on the true complexity of the ranking problem, capturing the item dependencies in terms of their feature representations. This was not possible with earlier matrix completion based tools used for this problem. We also prove an information theoretic lower bound on the required sample complexity for recovering the underlying ranking, which essentially shows the tightness of our proposed algorithms. article: Automatic annotation of temporal expressions is a research challenge of great interest in the field of information extraction. In this report, I describe a novel rule-based architecture, built on top of existing natural language processing tools, to automatically annotate temporal expressions in text data. The architecture consists of several modules, each responsible for a specific task in the annotation process. The first module is a pre-processing module that applies several text normalization techniques to standardize different textual representations of the same temporal expression. This normalization promotes consistency in the annotation process. The second module is a pattern matching module, where a set of regular expressions is defined to identify temporal expressions of interest in the text. This module also captures the type of temporal expression, for instance, whether it is absolute or relative. The third module is an inference module, which applies a set of rules to infer additional temporal expressions based on the identified expressions and the syntactic structure of the sentence. The final module is a post-processing module, where the identified temporal expressions are validated and refined to ensure accuracy and consistency. The architecture is evaluated on a dataset of news articles and achieves a high level of accuracy in temporal expression annotation. The proposed architecture can be extended to annotate other types of expressions, such as spatial and event expressions, in text data.

article: I hold this opinion for several reasons. First of all you have to sit too close to a large screen to take full advantage of the increase in resolution over 1080P. This vastly increases your horizontal viewing angle which will negatively impact your ability to see the entire movie or play a console game effectively. So ok, lets say you really like your nose up to the screen, that presents another problem, most living rooms are not setup to accommodate a TV that big or to sit that closely. There's a reason why 4K TVs are moving into the 85" range, because the average viewing distance of most people barely takes full advantage of most of the 1080p tvs in people's houses right now. Furthermore, to go to 4K you have to dump your plasma in favor of arguably inferior LCDLED technology that fails to produce effective black levels for the most part in comparison. The only technology on the horizon that can beat plasma in black levels is OLED. So we need a 85" OLED 4K TV to sit a comfortable 11 feet away, and that's going to be pricey and isn't even available yet. And that's saying nothing of the problem of upscaling older content that's likely to stay in 1080p for a considerable period of time. Upscaling that 1080p blu-ray, PS4 (which is already being upscaled to 1080P), or satellite image is going to make the picture blurry and inferior to a true 1:1 1080P image under the exact same conditions. In conclusion, 4K isn't ready for prime time, and likely won't be for at least another 5-10 years. The proper seating distance for a modern 1080P TV is about 1.6 times the diagonal length of the screen based on my research. I don't know what the comparable distance is exactly for 4K (guessing 1.0-1.1x since it's double the horizontal resolution), but the technical limitations are not going to accommodate most people. If you're looking to improve your AV experience most people would be vastly better served by getting a decent audio system for under 1K.

article: In this correspondence, we introduce a minimax regret criteria to the least squares problems with bounded data uncertainties and solve it using semi-definite programming. We investigate a robust minimax least squares problem where the objective is to find a solution that minimizes the worst-case regret among a set of possible datasets with bounded uncertainties. This type of problem arises in applications where the input data is subject to measurement errors or noise, and it is important to find a solution that is robust to these uncertainties. To solve this problem, we formulate it as a semi-definite programming problem, which is an efficient and scalable approach to solving optimization problems with convex constraints. In this approach, we introduce auxiliary variables to represent the worst-case regret, and we add constraints to ensure that the error in the solution is bounded by the data uncertainty. The resulting semi-definite programming problem can be solved using standard optimization software, and it provides a robust and efficient solution to the minimax least squares problem. Our approach has been applied to a variety of real-world problems, including image reconstruction, signal processing, and financial risk management, and it has been shown to be effective in improving the robustness and accuracy of the solution. Overall, the minimax regret criteria and the semi-definite programming approach provide a powerful tool for solving least squares problems with bounded data uncertainties, and they have broad applications in many areas of science and engineering.

Frequencies used for wifi is absorbed by air more than those used by phones.', "Cell phones really don't travel that far because there are cell towers everywhere. These towers are very tall, which allows them to pick up the very faint signals of cell phones around them. The size of the antenna isn't really relevant to reception. The placement of antennae (up high and without obstruction) are the important parts. Wifi routers operate on very high frequencies (2.4 gigahertz) which are more easily absorbed by walls,which is why they don't always cover a big house.," "First off, the antennas aren't the important part of this relationship; they are the length they need to be based on the frequency they are tuned to. What you are thinking of is the transceiver that the antenna is attached to, however I will put it into layman's terms: Putting it simply, there are 2 antennas in radio frequency communication: the transmitter antenna and the receiver antenna. If you think of the cell phone antenna as the receiver, and the cell tower as the transmitter, you have your 2 antennas. The connection between the 2 antennas needs a certain power level, and since the cell tower is nice and large and therefore providing the bulk of the necessary power, your cellphone antenna is much much smaller. With your router and computer, you are covering a smaller space, but the same principle applies. The router and computer are the 2 antennas, the router is providing the bulk of the necessary power, and the computer antenna can be smaller. Looping back around, cellphones actually have transceivers meaning they can send and receive information on radio frequencies, but the same ideas apply. There is an entire science and industry based on RF communication...my experience is based on that of RF design for sound engineering, basically wireless microphones, but the physics is the same for cell phones, satellite communication, ham radio, etc.,This probably won't get seen - but I'll give it a go anyway. It's a combination of a lot of factors that people have been talking about - but the key here is "combination." It's not just that your phone and the cell tower run at higher powers. They also know how to communicate with each other, maintain a constant link between each other and the cell tower has a "capacity" of number of phones it can talk to at one time; which cannot be broken - after this number it will not accept communications from another phone (for simplicity sake I'll state that your WiFi router is not limited in this way - it is limited, but not in the same way: that's a separate ELI5...) Imagine you and your friends out in a field and you've all got a set of alphabet flashcards of different sizes (from postage stamp size up to A1) each with their own colour. You tell your friends to go and stand in a line about 10m apart from each other all facing you and then use the cards to send you a message. You will respond to them with the cards of their own colour as you have a set of all the colours. The guy 10m from you holds up the A1 sized cards to start, and you're not able to see anyone else behind him because the card is in the way, so when you see the A1 sized card, you show your card to say you've got the message - but also that he needs to use a smaller sized card (the postage stamp one because you can read that from 10m away). This means that you and he can communicate (him using postage stamp sized cards, you using his coloured cards) While this is happening all you other friends are also holding up their A1 sized cards trying to get a message from you, but because you can't see them and so aren't responding, they keep trying the first part of the message. As the first guy changes to the postage stamp sized cards, you can see the 2nd guy and respond, tell him to use a smaller card, but bigger than the postage stamp so you can read it still from 20m away. This continues down the line until you can see all of your friends and they're all using different sized cards. They know which messages are for them because your cards are colour coded, and you've made sure that you can see all of their cards, so you can talk to them all. This means that your friend furthest away can still talk to you, even though he's a long way away. He's holding up the large card, which can be seen over all the smaller cards infront of it. This is like transmission power, phones nearer the tower are told to turn down their transmission power so that the tower can see what's happening "behind" them. This only works because the tower creates an unbroken link between itself and each phone that it is talking to, so it has a record of what phone is on what power and how to talk to that phone. Because the tower then knows what it is looking for to communicate with the phone, the phone doesn't need to be transmitting with such high power. There's a whole load more going on, if you're interested then drop me a PM and i'll explain more. TL,DR: It's not just 1 single thing that enables cell phones to work - there's a whole system designed specifically to get around range problems and a lot of smart things happening all at once.', "Alright, some seriously bullshit comments on this thread. This probably won't be seen by many but hopefully op sees it. Multiple factors are in play when considering cell phone signal vs wifi signal. TL;DR - A shit ton more powerlower frequenciesdirected antennasmuch farther range than your home wifi. 1) Frequency - Frequencies are waves. The lower the frequency, the bigger the wave is. The bigger the wave, the farther it travels before it is no longer usable. Why does Verizon have such good service in very rural areas? They have a lot of 850mhz spectrum, this means that a single cell tower can serve a much greater radius. Lower frequencies also impact penetration. The lower the frequency, the better it is at getting through buildings, trees, etc.... so less will interfere. 2) Directed antennas - Your wifi router at home has an omni directional antenna. This means it is sending out signal in all directions. Ever seen those DIY hacks that you put a parabola on a wifi antenna to get better signal in a certain area? That's why, directing more power in one direction will improve signal in that direction. Cell towers are not omni directional. Each cell tower has sectors, I've seen them go from 1 (rare), 3 (most common), to 6 (also rare). Each sector broadcasts its signal in a direction and if you could visualize how it's waves looked, you would see a cone. If you stand directly under a cell tower (assuming no other cell towers are near by) you will not get very good, or possibly any, signal. 3) Power - this is the biggest factor. This is the biggest factor. Cell towers use a LOT of power compared to your home wifi. A single cell is powerful enough that, if not turned off, will burn a worker operating directly in front of the cell. Put simple, you could possibly power a single or maybe a few cells with your home power connection but you wouldn't be able to power an entire cell tower. Source: I work for a cell phone provider on the networking side. I now deal with the core but I used to work with the cell towers. If you have any more questions about how a cell phone network works, feel free to ask. I love talking about it.," "So basically, wifi is specifically supposed to NOT have good range. WiFi operates on shared frequencies (2.4 ghz band has a few different channels, 5.8 ghz has more), so if it goes much past your houseapartment, you can interfere with your neighbor's wifi. If that happens, no one has wifi. -Because WiFi operates on shared radio frequencies, it's limited to very low power. The antennas at the tower are also really good. -The equipment at the tower can be several tens of thousands of dollars, whereas your average WiFi router is under 100 -Most towers are tall, which helps signal go further (gets around buildings, over trees, etc).," "There are a lot of cell base stations for your phone to talk to, they're very, very well situated, and they're somewhat more powerful than an average wifi AP. Tons of care and attention goes into antenna location, positioning, and characteristics. The tower is linked to an infrastructure and connected to a SP (service provider). And wifi opperates on a higher frequency, and can only travel so far, intentionally.','Well first of all not all of the wireless network is actually wireless when it comes to cell phones. article: Phillips wished for noise-cancelling earphones as he struggled to get some shuteye on the C-37A. Though he was at the aircraft's fore, the aft-located engines droned ceaselessly with a volume surprisingly loud for a civilian aircraft. True, he'd flown on Black Hawks, Chinooks, and Ospreys that were far louder than this Gulfstream, but those were for distances that did not necessitate sleep. For some reason this tiny civilian plane's engines could compete with those of C-17s and C-130s. He shifted around in his his too-small seat, wishing that Gulfstream had manufactured seats more suited to his large frame. Perhaps it wasn't Gulfstream that made these seats though; they definitely weren't standard given the purpose of this jet, maybe it was just another lowest bidder who made cramped seats for cheap on the taxpayer dime. Phillips sighed. At least he wasn't the guy in the back. Eyes closed, Phillips felt a tap on his shoulder. "Phillips. I just checked in on the satphone. We have a problem." His partner Platt awoke him from his attempted rest. Platt was an agreeable guy; it was Phillips' first op with him, but so far they'd managed to execute and deliver. So far. "Problem, what kind of problem? Phillips inquired, yawning. "Do we need to get landing permissions at a different site? Get in touch with Johnson, he can liaise with the folks at State and deal with it. It's a spring-floored cell for the guy no matter where he goes, doesn't make a difference to me." "No, not that." Platt said curtly. "They processed the pictures we sent in. There's a negative ID." "Negative?" Phillips asked. "Negative? What the fuck do you mean negative, we got the wrong guy? Why the fuck am I hearing about this now?" "Affirmative on that. We got the wrong guy. I'm unclear on the timeframe details of the discovery, but the destination COS wants us to resolve this issue quietly. He says to get creative; we don't need more diplomatic backlash." Platt replied. "We have 12 hours to execute on that, he's giving us full leverage." "Jesus, fuck." Phillips was not amused. They'd gone with a team and snatched this guy in a night raid, almost losing a guy in the process. There was a too-long stint at Bagram, and when they finally got the clearance to get on this plane, finally some dickwad at a desk comes back with a negative ID? What a goddamn waste. "Suggestions?" Platt asked impatiently. Phillips was beginning to like him less, but he didn't care enough to show it. In this profession, you could never like anyone too much. Phillips stood up, looking towards the aft of the plane. "Where are we right now? Geographically speaking," he asked. "Last I checked with the pilot twenty minutes ago, we're still over the Black Sea. ETA to site just over an hour." "Good. Tell the pilot to go down low and slow, and depressurize," Phillips ordered. "Depressurize?" Platt quizzically inquired. "You've never seen someone jump without a chute, have you?" Phillips asked.

article: Stacy quickly turned off the TV on her desk, shaken. She had it muted so the children could continue sleeping soundly on their mats, but the breaking news message was still clear. She glanced at the calendar. It was March 27th, certainly too early for an April Fool's joke, but what if the news station decided to run the story a little early? " The best plan of action is to lock your doors and remain inside until we receive word that the crisis has been adverted, " the closed captions said. Hesitantly, Stacy turned the television back on. The channel she was watching had gone to a commercial break, so she flipped to another local station. Images of sick people in the hospital flashed across the screen. People both young and old, bound to gurneys overflowing the halls with masks on their faces. Just this morning everything was fine, Stacy thought, this can't be real. She couldn't quite tell if they were alive or dead. The children were beginning to stir from their naps, but Stacy continued to sit there, completely oblivious to her classroom. Suddenly, the door burst open and she had to cover her mouth with her hand to silence the screen that almost came out. Her close friend and fellow teacher stood at the door. " Have you seen the news? " Harry asked, at a noise level one could consider rude if not given the current situation. " It has to be a joke, right? " Stacy stammered. Harry paused for a moment. " My wife just called. It's real. They're shutting down access to the hospital and barricading the streets in and out of town. " Harry's wife was a surgeon at the hospital. Stacy had met her once at a Christmas party. She seemed nice enough, but had a very serious and professional demeanor. She didn't seem like the kind of person to be a part of such a horrible prank. " Hold on, she's calling me again. " He quickly left. No, this can't be happening. This is like something out of a horror movie, Stacy thought. She turned up the television a little. A professionally dressed reporter filled her screen. It was obvious that she was uncomfortable standing so close to the hospital. " We have received confirmation that the virus is quickly spreading through contact with bodily fluids. There are reports that the mucus spread by sneezing is the most contagious, but we haven't received an official statement regarding that yet. Avoid anyone who may be sneezing and immediately vacate the vicinity. There have been reports of violent attacks from infected individuals. If possible, stay in your homes until further information is received. " A fair distance behind the reporter, Stacy could see a teenager make a quick, startled movement. Was that a sneeze? Everything after that happened so quickly. Stacy could see that the figure in the background was no more than sixteen, but his body movements were that of someone much older and much stronger. He jumped higher than humanly possible, landing on the reporter's back. He grabbed at her throat, and blood sprayed over the camera. The television went black. Reeling, Stacy tried to process what had happened. After a minute, she remembered where she was. The children! She needed to protect them at all costs. She locked the door and started covering the windows, following the same emergency procedures she always followed during her weekly drills. As she finished covering the windows, she turned back to her desk and heard the familiar rustling sound of the children waking. She supposed locking down her classroom woke them up. She decided to let them sleep a few more minutes, and went back to her desk, debating if she wanted to try turning the television to another station or not. She opened her desk drawer and found her purse. She grabbed her cell phone and looked for her sister's number. As she scrolled through her contacts list, she heard a quiet, but still audible sneeze. - As promised, Harry returned back to Stacy's classroom. Halfway there, he stopped. He could hear screaming and crying from the room. He rushed the door, but it wouldn't budge. Locked. Dammit! Harry tried to kick the door in, without much luck. The school had recently seen significant security renovations, and the doors were no longer the flimsy wood paneling they used to be. Without warning, the paper covering the small window on the door fell down. He could see - but not believe - what was on the other side. A child, such a sweet, innocent child, was chewing on what used to be Stacy. Harry choked, making a foreign guttural noise. The child slowly turned around, making eye contact with Harry.

article: In this paper, we theoretically address three fundamental problems involving deep convolutional networks regarding invariance, depth and hierarchy. We introduce the paradigm of Transformation Networks (TN) which are a direct generalization of Convolutional Networks (ConvNets). Theoretically, we show that TNs (and thereby ConvNets) are can be invariant to non-linear transformations of the input despite pooling over mere local translations. Our analysis provides clear insights into the increase in invariance with depth in these networks. Deeper networks are able to model much richer classes of transformations. We also find that a hierarchical architecture allows the network to generate invariance much more efficiently than a non-hierarchical network. Our results provide useful insight into these three fundamental problems in deep learning using ConvNets.

article: All traditional methods of computing shortest paths depend upon edge-relaxation where the cost of reaching a vertex from a source vertex is possibly decreased if that edge is used. We can also use algorithms such as Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford algorithm, and Floyd-Warshall algorithm to find the shortest path in a graph. These algorithms work by exploring the graph and keeping track of the shortest path found so far. Dijkstra's algorithm, for example, works by starting at the source vertex and exploring its neighbors. It then selects the vertex with the shortest distance from the source and explores its neighbors. This process continues until the desired destination vertex is reached. Bellman-Ford algorithm works by relaxing all edges in the graph repeatedly, checking if any improvements can still be made. This process is repeated until no further improvements can be made. Floyd-Warshall algorithm works by computing the shortest path between every pair of vertices in the graph, by repeatedly considering the intermediate vertices. All of these algorithms have different time and space complexities, and may be useful in different scenarios depending on the size and complexity of the graph.

To address this challenge, various methods have been proposed in the literature, including centralised training with decentralised execution (CTDE), which involves training a central critic that takes as input the observations and actions of all agents, but allowing the agents to act independently based on their own observations during execution. Another method is multi-agent actor-critic (MAAC), which uses a central critic to estimate the value function, but each agent has its own actor policy that is trained independently based on its own observations. MAAC also includes a consensus module that ensures that the agents' policies converge to a common solution during training. Other approaches to learning a CVF in MARL include decentralized value function (DVFs) and opponent modelling, which involves modelling the behaviour of other agents as opponents to improve the robustness of the learned CVF. Overall, learning a stable and generalizable CVF remains an active area of research in MARL, and there is no one-size-fits-all solution, as each approach has its own strengths and limitations depending on the characteristics of the environment and the agents involved.
